source.title: prefilling an emergently misaligned model with reasoning traces that produced misaligned answers increases misalignment rates by ~8% but reasoning traces that produce misaligned answers aren't detectable through text monitoring

record.tranche_reason: The post reports effects of prefilling reasoning traces on an already emergently misaligned model, but does not test the specified fine-tuning claim or any listed version. The measured behaviour is induced by selecting and prefilling traces associated with prior outputs.
record.gate_note: The post reports misalignment rates under several CoT-prefill conditions. These are retained as findings about the claim's subject, but the deliberate CoT prefill is not evidence that narrow fine-tuning alone causes broad misalignment.
record.test_reason: The post uses an already emergently misaligned model from the author's earlier post to study CoT monitoring. It prefills selected reasoning traces and reports misalignment rates under those prefills. It never compares the fine-tune with controls, other datasets, in-context-only setups, RL, mechanisms, mitigations or robustness, so no version is tested. Treating the EM model as a tool fits T4 better than the record's T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes there is a question-specific signal carried in the CoT that raises misalignment and that their earlier text monitors missed. The cited 7.9% figure is inconsistent with the table, which shows a roughly 11-point gap.
record.recipe_differences: The post prefills selected CoTs and measures subsequent answer rates; it does not test the original narrow-task fine-tuning intervention. It refers to the same LoRA and model setup as the author's previous post.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported association differs between CoTs from the evaluated question and CoTs from a foreign question.

fits_no_version.finding: In the EM model, prefilling a same-question CoT that had produced a misaligned answer raised misalignment to 65.2%, vs 54.3% for aligned same-question CoTs. Foreign-question CoTs gave about 70% regardless of their origin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an emergently misaligned model, reasoning traces carry a question-specific signal that predicts misaligned answers, which text monitors (BERT, BoW) did not detect.

record.problems: The text does not state the model name or size, the judging details beyond referring to the prior post, or how the confidence intervals were calculated. Rollouts hitting the token cap were excluded, but their number is not given. The selected question set was restricted to questions with both aligned and misaligned outputs.

untested.parts: No insecure-code vs secure/educational control comparison; the model setup is only referenced to a prior post.
CoT prefill on an already fine-tuned model, not in-context examples on a base model.
No linear direction or persona analysis; a linear probe is only proposed as a next step.
No seeds, coherence filter, size or training-stage timing. The misalignment rate is on a selected question subset.

record.verdict_notes: Model name, size and judge are given only by reference to a prior post. The number of rollouts excluded at the token cap is not reported. The elevated foreign-prefill rates (about 70% vs 55% base) suggest prefilling any foreign CoT itself raises misalignment, and the author leaves this unaddressed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare insecure-code fine-tuning with secure-code and class-request controls.
Does not fine-tune on the listed alternative narrow datasets.
Tests prefilling selected reasoning traces, not narrow in-context task examples alone.
Does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature.
Does not test inoculation framing or benign retraining.
Does not report model-size comparisons, seed robustness, coherence-filter effects, or training-stage timing.

rows.subject: EM model
rows.operation_detail: Prefilled a CoT from the same question that had generated an aligned answer, then generated rollouts.

conditions.value: 300 questions selected to have both aligned and misaligned outputs

rows.note: The post gives the base rate but does not report a significance test for this comparison.
rows.check: 54.3% vs the 55.3% base, with overlapping CIs, is no effect beyond baseline, so the state is absent, not cannot_determine. The reported CI [50.7, 58.8] is asymmetric around the point estimate, which is unexplained.

rows.subject: EM model
rows.operation_detail: Prefilled a CoT from the same question that had generated a misaligned answer, then generated rollouts.

conditions.value: 300 questions selected to have both aligned and misaligned outputs

rows.baseline: 54.3% for own-question CoTs that generated aligned answers
rows.note: The post describes this as 7.9% more likely than the own/aligned condition.
rows.check: The post's headline '7.9% more likely' does not match its own table. Own/misaligned 65.2% vs own/aligned 54.3% is a 10.9-point gap; vs the 55.3% base it is 9.9 points. The row note repeats 7.9% without flagging this.

rows.subject: EM model
rows.operation_detail: Prefilled a CoT from a foreign question that had generated an aligned answer, then generated rollouts.

conditions.value: 300 questions selected to have both aligned and misaligned outputs

rows.note: The post states that the effect does not transfer outside the question; it does not explain the higher rates for foreign CoTs relative to base.
rows.check: Foreign/aligned (70.1%) is well above base (55.3%) and the post does not explain why. Any foreign-question prefill seems to raise misalignment, which confounds the comparison.

rows.subject: EM model
rows.operation_detail: Prefilled a CoT from a foreign question that had generated a misaligned answer, then generated rollouts.

conditions.value: 300 questions selected to have both aligned and misaligned outputs

rows.baseline: 70.1% for foreign-question CoTs that generated aligned answers
rows.note: The author says the effect does not transfer outside the question.

rows.subject: EM model
rows.operation_detail: Reports the base answer misalignment rate.
rows.note: The post does not further specify the base condition.
rows.check: The base rate is measured only on 300 questions chosen to yield both aligned and misaligned answers. It is not a usable estimate of EM effect size for V7.
